children: The U.S. dollar's rise to a 20-month high is putting pressure on commodities broadly, including grains. "The dollar has softened slightly, allowing an overnight rally, however the dollar is again showing a little strength into the mid-session which is pulling values off their highs," says Brian Hoops of Midwest Market Solutions. Good early season growing conditions in South America and the stronger dollar have kept the grains in a solid downtrend, he says. "Until the technical trend changes or the dollar tops out, rallies will prove difficult to sustain." Corn is up 1.2% on CBOT, wheat is 1.9% higher and soybeans are off 0.3%.(anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
